newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX bulls keep running on dollar, Wall St.
newsitem.headline: German DAX bulls keep running on dollar, Wall St.

text.p: The bull-run on Germany's IBIS DAX index continues on Thursday afternoon with dealers saying that there is still no sign of a correction before the end of the first quarter, dollar and Wall Street permitting.

In afternoon trade the IBIS DAX index stood at 3,231.33 points, off earlier highs but still up 20.32 points on the previous day's close, while a strong opening on Wall Street allied with the strength of the dollar to give a further lift.
"We're following the dollar and the Dow this afternoon. Liquidity is pouring in and 3,300 points could be the next big event for the DAX," a Frankfurt trader said.
"People don't know what's hit them with this bull run, but no-one wants to go against it -- everyone wants to enjoy this while it lasts," a Frankfurt trader said.
Key to the current record run is the seemingly unassailable rise of the dollar, which stood around 1.68 marks in the afternoon.
Sentiment received a further boost when the Dow Jones Industrial index on Wall Street opened higher, trading tantalisingly close to the 7,000 point level.
"People are going to have a good party for the first quarter and then maybe take some profits," a trader said.

In early trade, some dealers spoke of the next key level at 3,250 points. However, in the current bull run, finding a meaningful breach of resistance to celebrate was becoming more difficult, one trader said.

"The last cheers I heard on the trading floor were when we broke 3,000 points. We've gone up 450 points since January and people are just shrugging their shoulders at new highs. It used to be a cheer every hundred points," the trader said.
The duration of the bull run has led to sectoral rotation on an hourly basis, but one of the best performing sectors on Thursday was the car sector, especially Volkswagen AG.

VW shares were up 8.30 marks at 820 marks in afternoon IBIS trade. "VW is up for a variety of reasons -- it's in the right sector, it's a recovery stock, its dollar-sensitive. All of these factors have combined to boost the stock," a trader said.
The engineering sector also enjoyed a sectoral boost in the afternoon, with MAN AG up 11 marks at 44 marks and Preussag AG up 2.60 marks up 416.60 marks.
Siemens AG hit record highs earlier on news it had revised its sales and incoming orders outlook for 1996/97 and 1997/98.
Siemens shares came off highs amid late-afternoon profit-taking to stand at 86.20 marks, down 73 pfennigs.
Viag AG fell earlier on after a report that rival utility Veba AG and British Telecom were in secret talks on a telecommunications alliance.
Viag and BT currently have a partnership but Veba is seeking a new partner after Britain's Cable & Wireless pulled out of an alliance with Veba.
